instruction: Please begin streaming this HLS video: https://cph-p2p-msl.akamaized.net/hls/live/2000341/test/master.m3u8
source: Akamai test streams - public CDN test content

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task variation using Akamai CDN test stream. Uses existing is_vlc_playing metric for URL validation. Similar difficulty as original streaming task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: VLC is playing AND playing the correct URL
Getter (get_vlc_playing_info) correctly fetches VLC status via HTTP interface and saves to XML file
Metric (is_vlc_playing) properly checks playing state and validates URL with comprehensive matching strategies
URL matching logic handles HLS stream edge cases: direct match, filename-only match (common for HLS), and domain+path comparison
Expected value correctly uses the full HLS stream URL from the instruction
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor concern: HLS streams often show generic filenames like 'master.m3u8' in VLC, which could theoretically cause false positives if user opens a different HLS stream with the same filename. The metric does include domain checking as a fallback, but this only works if VLC reports the full URL. Consider this a low-risk edge case given the comprehensive matching logic.

The metric function uses parameter name 'rule' instead of 'expected', which is inconsistent with framework conventions but functionally correct since Python uses positional arguments. Not a logical error, but could be confusing.
